Messages.Author: Kushiel
Messages.Body:
1) Stupid question time: The controller of the acting vampire chooses all of the targets of Sowing Dissension, correct?

2) Can Sowing Dissension be played if there are one or more other players who have no ready untapped vampires younger than the acting vampire?

2a) If the answer to #2 is "yes," what happens if a methuselah has no ready untapped vampires when Sowing Dissension successfully resolves?

2b) If the answer to #2 is "no," does Sowing Dissension fizzle if one of the selected targets becomes tapped between the announcement of the action (including its targets) and before the action resolves, even if the action was otherwise successful?

Sowing Dissension
Requires a ready anarch.
Each other Methuselah taps an untapped ready younger vampire he or she controls. If this action is blocked by a non-titled vampire, the acting anarch can burn 1 blood to cancel combat and untap.

Messages.Author: Juggernaut1981
Messages.Body:
1) Not so sure, Sowing Dissension appears to target the Methuselahs and compels them to take an action if resolved. "Each other Methuselah..." instead of "Choose one younger minion controlled by each other Methuselah". I'd want to have Pascal (or maybe an old LSJ ruling) confirm just what the target of the action is.

2) If the action targets the Methuselahs then it is valid regardless, the Methuselah is compelled to take an action which they cannot successfully resolve and it fizzles for that Methuselah. Rather like Political Actions such as "Peace Treaty".

Retired Baron of Sydney, Australia, 418

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> Kushiel wrote:
> 1) Stupid question time: The controller of the acting vampire chooses all of the targets of Sowing Dissension, correct?
>
The targets of Sowing Dissension are the Methuselah, not the minions. So you have nothing to choose when you announce the action. Upon resolution, each Methuselah will choose an "an untapped ready younger vampire he or she controls" and tap it.

> Kushiel wrote:
> 2) Can Sowing Dissension be played if there are one or more other players who have no ready untapped vampires younger than the acting vampire?
>
Yes. But it will have no effect for these Methuselahs.

> Kushiel wrote:
> 2a) If the answer to #2 is "yes," what happens if a methuselah has no ready untapped vampires when Sowing Dissension successfully resolves?
>
Nothing for him.

> Kushiel wrote:
> 2b) If the answer to #2 is "no," does Sowing Dissension fizzle if one of the selected targets becomes tapped between the announcement of the action (including its targets) and before the action resolves, even if the action was otherwise successful?
>
Moot.

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
> PetriWessman wrote:
> Just to make sure: Sowing Dissention is still considered to be an undirected action, right?
>
Not any more, since 08/08/08.
groups.google.com/d/msg/rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad/1jW6GXrIRSU/8QTYL98kB0gJ
>
> Some actions target more than one thing, some without the ability to
> individually control the selection, like Edged Illusion or Jaroslav Pascek's
> special ability. If one or more of the targets cannot be targeted (because of
> Trophy: Safe Passage, Sleep Unseen, or Reality, for example), the action can
> still be taken, and it will simply have no effect on the things it cannot target
> (and have the normal effect on the allowable targets).
>
> Each of the actual targets is considered a target, which means that effects like
> Hide's "the action fails" or Talley's "+1 intercept" can be used if any one (or
> more) of the targets would be enough to enable the effect.
>
> If one of the multiple targets becomes ineligible during the course of the
> action, then it's handled just as if it had always been ineligible. The action
> resolves on the remaining targets as above.
>
Sowing Dissension is a  action against all (other) Methuselahs
